history.title: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED: the convolution ring was exactly conv_k slots wide, but a speculative pass writes TILE rows ahead - so a rejected pass evicted the row the next pass's first convolution still needed. Ring is now (conv_k + TILE).next_power_of_two(), mask-indexed. plain vs spec is now byte-identical over 3 prompts x 300 tokens

gates.G2: parity 6/6 + spec==plain byte-for-byte on 3 prompts x 300 tokens

evidence.root_cause: the pass at position p writes ring slots for p, p+1, p+2; the slot for p+2 is the same slot as p-2 (p+2 = p-2 + conv_k), so the second draft evicted the row for p-2. With k=0 the next pass starts at p+1 and its row 0 convolves over {p-2, p-1, p, p+1}, reading the discarded draft in place of p-2
evidence.why_it_hid: both extra rows are real rows of the same sequence, so the corruption is a one-row-old convolution input - small enough to normally change nothing, which is why I twice mislabelled the resulting divergence as floating-point noise at a near-tie
evidence.fix: ring is (conv_k + TILE).next_power_of_two() = 8 slots, indexed with a mask so the kernel costs exactly what it did before
evidence.method: QW_NO_ACCEPT=1 (force k=0) made the rejection path the only path and turned a rare corruption into divergence at token 4; QW_TILE_CHECK proves the tiled arithmetic is bit-exact (max|dlogit|=0.0). Together they separate wrong arithmetic from wrong state
evidence.tile4: built and tested: correct but strictly worse - acceptance 75.5%->55.6%, tokens/pass 2.51->2.67, materially higher pass cost. TILE=3 stays
evidence.thermal: box throttled from back-to-back model loads (plain decode 87 ms/token vs 24.6 ms in round 031); spec/plain ratio 1.38x unchanged; absolute numbers to be re-measured in a cool window

evidence.change: new kernels conv1d_silu_ring_tile (grid conv_dim*TILE, row r reads ring slot slot0+r) and rmsnorm_nw_tile (grid hk*TILE*NT, threadgroup flattened to (row, head)); forward2's GDN branch is now three phases - qkv per row into its ring slot, then one convolution and two norms for the tile, then the recurrence row by row because it is sequential in the state
evidence.gate_bug_caught: an intermediate run of the byte-identical gate reported IDENTICAL for both prompts because gen had died on an MSL compile error and the two EMPTY outputs compared equal; the gate now asserts the token count
evidence.msl_constraint: MSL rejects a kernel that mixes vector thread-position bindings with scalar ones - the flattened 1D grid is a requirement, not a style choice
evidence.ab: order-alternating A/B in one cool window, 4 pairs: 0.987, 0.967, 1.001, 0.953 => median 0.977 (~2.3% faster). Best readings 41.31 (new) vs 40.62 (old) tok/s
evidence.where_time_goes: a pass emits 2.51 tokens in ~61 ms vs a plain step's ~37 ms for one token; the pass moves ~13.5 GB of weights + ~1.9 GB of lm_head (all three rows need logits to verify) + ~1.4 GB of MTP drafts = ~16.8 GB in 61 ms = ~275 GB/s, while the plain step already reaches ~364 GB/s on the same weights, so the speculative pass is NOT at the bandwidth ceiling and has real headroom
evidence.next_suspect: the three-row accumulator in the tiled GEMV costing occupancy; a pass matching the plain step's bandwidth efficiency would land near 60 tok/s

history.next: attack the tiled GEMV's bandwidth efficiency: measure occupancy/register pressure for the k=3 kernel, try wider threadgroups or splitting the accumulator, and re-run the order-alternating A/B. Keep the byte-identical gate (now asserting token counts) as the correctness gate

next: throughput margin: the bar is met only on a median (38.03 dip), so cut dispatches per pass. Order: batch conv1d_silu_ring and rmsnorm_nw across the tile rows, batch gdn_step's serial rows, fold ewise_add into the following rmsnorm, fold silu_mul into the up-GEMV, fold the q/k norms together
